```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Warnings stay visible so convergence or rank-deficiency problems show up.
# Cached chunks are invalidated when either input file changes.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE, autodep = TRUE,
  cache.extra = unname(tools::md5sum(c("adult24.csv", "adult25.csv")))
)

library(splines)
library(xgboost)
library(PRROC)
library(survey)
library(grpreg)
library(parallel)

options(survey.lonely.psu = "adjust", width = 110)

# Parallel steps use at most 4 worker processes (fewer on small machines).
# One BLAS/OpenMP thread per process avoids oversubscription; these
# variables take effect only if set before R starts using BLAS, so they can
# also be set in ~/.Renviron.
n_workers <- max(1L, min(4L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L))
Sys.setenv(OMP_NUM_THREADS = "1", OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS = "1",
           VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS = "1")

# Stop if any parallel task failed or returned nothing (mclapply otherwise
# returns the error object silently).
check_workers <- function(results) {
  failed <- vapply(results, function(r) is.null(r) || inherits(r, "try-error"),
                   logical(1))
  if (any(failed)) {
    stop("Parallel task(s) ", paste(which(failed), collapse = ", "), " failed: ",
         paste(unique(vapply(results[failed], function(r) {
           if (is.null(r)) "no result returned" else as.character(r)
         }, character(1))), collapse = " | "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  results
}
```

# Overview

**Outcome.** `VIRAPP12M_A`: had a video or phone appointment with a doctor
or other health professional in the past 12 months (1 = Yes, 2 = No; 7/8/9
excluded).

**Design.** The analysis has two phases.

* **Development (2024 only).** The 2024 NHIS Sample Adult file is split
  80/20 into training and test sets (stratified by outcome), with 5-fold
  cross-validation inside the training set. Data-based screening (item
  coverage), variable selection, tuning and model fitting use the training
  set only. The coding dictionary was drafted from NHIS conventions while
  viewing predictor distributions in the full 2024 file, but no outcome
  information. From the 2025 file, only the list of variable names is read,
  to restrict candidates to items fielded in both years. The 2024 test set
  is used only to evaluate models whose form was fixed beforehand.
* **Temporal validation (2025).** The fixed models are evaluated on the
  2025 file, an independent cross-sectional sample of different
  respondents collected one year later. Variable availability and coding
  are checked before evaluation; the models are not refit or modified.

**Variable selection.**

1. *Rule-based screening* of every 2024 item: fielded in 2025; at least 90%
   of 2024 training respondents with a substantive answer; not a
   survey-administration field; not redundant with a retained item; worded
   the same way in both years; and not an item whose answer a telehealth
   visit in the reference period can produce (counseling that may be
   delivered by video or phone, online contact with a provider).
2. *Outcome-proxy diagnostic.* Items that a telehealth visit cannot
   produce but that may stand in for the outcome (in-person care use,
   online health activity, treatment, prevention, cost barriers, COVID-19
   history) are added one at a time to the theory-based model on the
   training data. Items contributing more than the strongest theory-based
   predictor are excluded. Unflagged care-use and access items are kept
   aside as *borderline* items for a sensitivity analysis only, because
   they measure care seeking itself; unflagged COVID-19 history remains an
   ordinary candidate.
3. *Coding.* Screened items are coded with an explicit dictionary (valid
   codes, nonresponse codes, skip meaning, category grouping, reference
   level); theory-based items are coded in `prepare_nhis()`. Codes,
   labels, universes and question wording were checked against the 2024
   and 2025 Sample Adult codebooks (`codebook_verification.csv`).
4. *Statistical selection* among all candidates, with no item forced in:
   bidirectional stepwise selection by BIC starting from the intercept-only
   model, with group lasso (every item penalized) as a cross-check and
   repeated half-sample selection to assess stability. The five covariates
   of the project dashboard's association model (age, insurance, education,
   Internet access, self-rated health) are part of the theory-based set
   and are treated like every other candidate. Nested cross-validation
   evaluates the selection and fitting steps *given the screened candidate
   set*; screening, coding and the outcome-proxy diagnostic are done once
   beforehand and are not repeated inside folds.
5. *Two comparisons*, with a constant (prevalence-only) model as the lower
   reference. (a) Full theory-based (Andersen) model vs stepwise BIC within
   the same 22 items: can the theory-based set be simplified? (b)
   Theory-based models vs models built from the wider screened pool
   (stepwise BIC, group lasso, XGBoost): how much do more items and
   different methods add?

**Theory-based set.** Andersen's behavioral model is a conceptual
framework without a standard variable list. The 22 items are one
operationalization: commonly used predisposing, enabling and need measures
available in both NHIS years. It is not a validated standard set.
Urban-rural classification, a common enabling factor, was missing from the
initial specification by oversight and was added afterwards; because
earlier analyses had already shown it to be a strong predictor, this
addition was not made blind to the data.

**Primary model.** The main-effects stepwise BIC model was fixed as the
primary model before any test-set or 2025 evaluation. It is a compromise
between parsimony and predictive performance, not the best-predicting
model: BIC does not directly optimize out-of-sample log loss, stepwise
search finds a good model along its search path rather than a guaranteed
optimum, and fewer items do not by themselves make a model easier to use
in practice. More flexible models (group lasso, including its sparser
1-SE version, and gradient boosting) are reported for comparison.
Interaction and borderline-item analyses are exploratory and do not change
the primary model.

**Weights.** Models are fit unweighted as the baseline, and
discrimination and accuracy are reported both unweighted (performance in
the analysis sample) and survey-weighted (performance for the U.S. adult
population represented by the complete-case sample). A sensitivity
analysis refits the primary formula with survey weights. Bootstrap
intervals resample primary sampling units within strata and apply to the
*unweighted* metrics of the already-fitted models; they reflect the
clustered sample but not uncertainty from model training or selection,
and they are not a full design-based inference for weighted metrics. The
2025 weighted calibration gap uses a design-based (Taylor linearization)
interval from the `survey` package.

Run time is roughly 1.5 to 2 hours (nested cross-validation and repeated
selection dominate). Slow chunks are cached after the first knit, and
parallel steps run on macOS and Linux.

# Data preparation

## Theory-based predictors

The same function prepares both survey years, so the 2025 validation data
use the 2024 coding rules.

```{r prepare-function}
raw_fields <- c(
  "VIRAPP12M_A", "AGEP_A", "NOTCOV_A", "PRIVATE_A", "EDUCP_A",
  "ACCSSINT_A", "PHSTAT_A", "SEX_A", "HISPALLP_A", "REGION", "MARITAL_A",
  "NATUSBORN_A", "EMPWRKLSW1_A", "POVRATTC_A", "HYPEV_A", "DIBEV_A",
  "ASEV_A", "COPDEV_A", "CANEV_A", "ARTHEV_A", "DEPEV_A", "ANXEV_A",
  "DISAB3_A", "WTFA_A", "PSTRAT", "PPSU"
)

# The five covariates of the project dashboard's association model; part of
# the theory-based set, with no special status in selection.
dashboard_predictors <- c("age", "insurance", "education", "internet", "health")
added_predictors <- c(
  "sex", "race_eth", "region", "marital", "us_born", "worked_last_week",
  "pov_ratio", "hypertension", "diabetes", "asthma", "copd", "cancer",
  "arthritis", "depression", "anxiety", "disability"
)
expanded_predictors <- c(dashboard_predictors, added_predictors)

# Yes (1) / No (2) items; refused, not ascertained, don't know -> NA.
yes_no <- function(x) {
  factor(x, levels = c(2, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))
}

# Items with >= 1% "not ascertained" keep an explicit Unknown category.
with_unknown <- function(x, codes, labels) {
  out <- rep("Unknown", length(x))
  for (i in seq_along(codes)) out[x %in% codes[i]] <- labels[i]
  factor(out, levels = c(labels, "Unknown"))
}

prepare_nhis <- function(raw) {
  stopifnot(all(raw_fields %in% names(raw)))
  rows <- which(raw$VIRAPP12M_A %in% c(1, 2))
  d <- raw[rows, ]

  insurance <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(d))
  insured <- d$NOTCOV_A %in% 2
  insurance[d$NOTCOV_A %in% 1] <- "Uninsured"
  insurance[insured & d$PRIVATE_A %in% c(1, 2)] <- "Any private coverage"
  insurance[insured & d$PRIVATE_A %in% 3] <- "Public / other, no private"

  education <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(d))
  education[d$EDUCP_A %in% 0:2] <- "Less than high school"
  education[d$EDUCP_A %in% 3:4] <- "High school / GED"
  education[d$EDUCP_A %in% 5:7] <- "Some college / associate"
  education[d$EDUCP_A %in% 8:10] <- "Bachelor's or higher"

  race_eth <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(d))
  race_eth[d$HISPALLP_A %in% 1] <- "Hispanic"
  race_eth[d$HISPALLP_A %in% 2] <- "NH White"
  race_eth[d$HISPALLP_A %in% 3] <- "NH Black"
  race_eth[d$HISPALLP_A %in% 4] <- "NH Asian"
  race_eth[d$HISPALLP_A %in% 5:7] <- "NH other / multiple"

  data.frame(
    telehealth = as.integer(d$VIRAPP12M_A == 1),
    # AGEP_A 85 = 85 or older (top-coded); 97/98/99 -> NA.
    age = ifelse(d$AGEP_A %in% 18:85, d$AGEP_A, NA_integer_),
    insurance = factor(insurance, levels = c(
      "Any private coverage", "Public / other, no private", "Uninsured"
    )),
    education = factor(education, levels = c(
      "Bachelor's or higher", "Some college / associate",
      "High school / GED", "Less than high school"
    )),
    internet = factor(d$ACCSSINT_A, levels = c(1, 2),
                      labels = c("Internet access", "No internet access")),
    health = factor(d$PHSTAT_A, levels = 1:5,
                    labels = c("Excellent", "Very good", "Good", "Fair", "Poor")),
    sex = factor(d$SEX_A, levels = 1:2, labels = c("Male", "Female")),
    race_eth = factor(race_eth, levels = c(
      "NH White", "Hispanic", "NH Black", "NH Asian", "NH other / multiple"
    )),
    region = factor(d$REGION, levels = 1:4,
                    labels = c("Northeast", "Midwest", "South", "West")),
    marital = with_unknown(d$MARITAL_A, 1:3,
                           c("Married", "Living with partner", "Neither")),
    us_born = with_unknown(d$NATUSBORN_A, 1:2, c("Yes", "No")),
    # Edited recode (accounts for temporary absence and unpaid family work);
    # code 9 (don't know) becomes the Unknown category.
    worked_last_week = with_unknown(d$EMPWRKLSW1_A, 1:2, c("Yes", "No")),
    # 2024 top-codes the ratio at 11; apply the same cap to every year.
    pov_ratio = pmin(d$POVRATTC_A, 11),
    hypertension = yes_no(d$HYPEV_A),
    diabetes = yes_no(d$DIBEV_A),
    asthma = yes_no(d$ASEV_A),
    copd = yes_no(d$COPDEV_A),
    cancer = yes_no(d$CANEV_A),
    arthritis = yes_no(d$ARTHEV_A),
    depression = yes_no(d$DEPEV_A),
    anxiety = yes_no(d$ANXEV_A),
    disability = yes_no(d$DISAB3_A),
    survey_weight = d$WTFA_A,
    survey_stratum = d$PSTRAT,
    survey_psu = d$PPSU,
    source_row = rows
  )
}
```

## Item labels, screening rules and coding dictionary

Item labels and the coding dictionary were written from NHIS conventions
and then checked item by item against the 2024 and 2025 Sample Adult
codebooks (codes, labels, universes, question wording; page references in
`codebook_verification.csv`). The dictionary is exported to
`coding_dictionary.csv`. For theory-based items, the dictionary documents
the codes used for screening coverage; their analysis coding is done in
`prepare_nhis()`.

```{r screening-rules}

# telehealth prediction analysis.
#
# The coding dictionary below was written from NHIS conventions and the
# codes observed in the 2024 file. Entries marked "verify" in particular
# must be checked against the 2024 and 2025 Sample Adult codebooks; the
# dictionary is exported to coding_dictionary.csv for that review.

core_raw <- c("AGEP_A", "NOTCOV_A", "PRIVATE_A", "EDUCP_A", "ACCSSINT_A", "PHSTAT_A")
# Theory-based items coded by the dictionary rather than prepare_nhis().
theory_dictionary_raw <- c("URBRRL23")
added16_raw <- c("SEX_A", "HISPALLP_A", "REGION", "MARITAL_A", "NATUSBORN_A",

# ---- Coding dictionary --------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry lists the analysis categories ("groups") and the NHIS codes in
# each, the codes treated as nonresponse (refused, not ascertained, don't
# know), the meaning of a blank (NA) when the item was skipped by design,
# how nonresponse is handled, and the reference category. Nonresponse gets
# its own "Missing" category when it is about 1% or more of 2024
# respondents; otherwise it is assigned to the most common category.
item <- function(groups, missing = c(7, 8, 9), skip = NULL,
                 nonresponse = "Missing", ref = names(groups)[1],
                 type = "categorical", note = "") {
  stopifnot(ref %in% names(groups),
            nonresponse %in% c("Missing", "Exclude", names(groups)))
  list(groups = groups, missing = missing, skip = skip,
       nonresponse = nonresponse, ref = ref, type = type, note = note)
}
yes_no_item <- function(nonresponse = "No", ref = "No", yes = 1, no = 2, ...) {
  item(setNames(list(yes, no), c("Yes", "No")), nonresponse = nonresponse,
       ref = ref, type = "binary", ...)
}
difficulty_item <- function(merge_cannot = FALSE, ...) {
  groups <- if (merge_cannot) {
    list("No difficulty" = 1, "Some difficulty" = 2,
         "A lot of difficulty or cannot do" = 3:4)
  } else {
    list("No difficulty" = 1, "Some difficulty" = 2,
         "A lot of difficulty" = 3, "Cannot do at all" = 4)
  }
  item(groups, nonresponse = "No difficulty", type = "ordinal", ...)
}
frequency_item <- function(...) {
  item(list("Never" = 5, "Daily" = 1, "Weekly" = 2, "Monthly" = 3,
            "A few times a year" = 4), type = "ordinal", ...)
}

dictionary_codes <- function(entry) unlist(entry$groups, use.names = FALSE)

# Dictionary in long form, for review against the codebooks.
dictionary_table <- function() {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(coding_dictionary), function(v) {
    e <- coding_dictionary[[v]]
    data.frame(
      variable = v, label = unname(variable_labels[v]), type = e$type,
      category = names(e$groups),
      nhis_codes = vapply(e$groups, function(g) {
        if (length(g) > 4 && all(diff(g) == 1)) sprintf("%g-%g", min(g), max(g))
        else paste(g, collapse = ",")
      }, character(1)),
      reference = names(e$groups) == e$ref,
      nonresponse_codes = paste(e$missing, collapse = ","),
      nonresponse_handling = e$nonresponse,
      skip_meaning = if (is.null(e$skip)) "" else e$skip,
      note = e$note
    )
  }))
}

# Coverage: share of respondents with a substantive answer. Dictionary codes
# are used when available; other items fall back to NHIS reserve-code
# conventions (7/8/9, 97/98/99, ...), which is approximate.
reserve_codes <- function(x) {
  v <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (!length(v)) return(numeric(0))
  d <- nchar(as.character(floor(max(v))))
  top <- 10^d - c(3, 2, 1)
  others <- setdiff(unique(v), top)
  if (length(others) && max(others) >= 10^d - 3) numeric(0) else top
}

item_coverage <- function(v, x) {
  e <- coding_dictionary[[v]]
  if (!is.null(e)) {
    if (e$type == "continuous") {
      g <- e$groups[[1]]
      return(mean(!is.na(x) & x >= min(g) & x <= max(g) & !(x %in% e$missing)))
    }
    return(mean(x %in% dictionary_codes(e)))
  }
  mean(!is.na(x) & !(x %in% reserve_codes(x)))
}

# Screening uses the 2024 data and only the *names* of the 2025 variables
# (which items were fielded in 2025). No 2025 values or outcomes are read.
screen_variables <- function(raw_2024, names_2025, min_coverage = 0.90) {
  outcome_24 <- raw_2024$VIRAPP12M_A %in% c(1, 2)
  vars <- setdiff(names(raw_2024), "VIRAPP12M_A")

  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(vars, function(v) {
    x <- raw_2024[[v]][outcome_24]
    data.frame(
      variable = v,
      coverage_2024 = if (is.numeric(x)) round(item_coverage(v, x), 3) else NA_real_,
      coverage_basis = if (v %in% names(coding_dictionary)) "dictionary" else
        "reserve-code convention (approximate)",
      share_nonblank_2024 = round(mean(!is.na(x)), 3)
    )
  }))
  out$fielded_2025 <- out$variable %in% names_2025

  low_coverage <- is.na(out$coverage_2024) | out$coverage_2024 < min_coverage
  v <- out$variable

  # Rules are applied in this order and a later rule overrides an earlier
  # one, so the list runs from lowest to highest priority. Theory-based
  # items are kept regardless of coverage (their coverage is reported in the
  # Rmd); final decisions for uncertain items are set after the
  # outcome-proxy diagnostic.
  decision <- rep("Excluded: not reviewed", length(v))
  rules <- list(
    list(v %in% names(coding_dictionary), "Candidate: new"),
    list(v %in% setdiff(uncertain_raw, uncertain_candidate_raw),
         "Uncertain: outcome-proxy check"),
    list(low_coverage, "Excluded: 2024 coverage < 90% (skip pattern)"),
    list(v %in% unverified_raw, "Excluded: label not verified"),
    list(v %in% too_rare_raw, "Excluded: too few respondents in a category"),
    list(v %in% admin_raw, "Excluded: survey administration"),
    list(v %in% redundant_raw, "Excluded: redundant"),
    list(v %in% not_comparable_raw, "Excluded: wording changed in 2025"),
    list(v %in% leakage_raw, "Excluded: answer can come from a telehealth visit"),
    list(v %in% c(core_raw, added16_raw, theory_dictionary_raw),
         "Candidate: theory-based set"),
    list(!out$fielded_2025, "Excluded: not fielded in 2025")
  )
  for (rule in rules) decision[rule[[1]]] <- rule[[2]]
  out$decision <- decision
  out$label <- unname(ifelse(v %in% names(variable_labels), variable_labels[v], ""))
  out[order(out$decision, out$variable),
      c("variable", "label", "decision", "coverage_2024", "coverage_basis",
        "share_nonblank_2024", "fielded_2025")]
}

# ---- Coding --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Apply the dictionary. The rules are fixed in advance and are not learned
# from the data, so the same coding applies inside every CV fold and in 2025.
code_item <- function(x, e, v = "", on_unknown = c("error", "warning")) {
  on_unknown <- match.arg(on_unknown)
  unknown <- !is.na(x) & !(x %in% c(dictionary_codes(e), e$missing))
  if (any(unknown)) {
    msg <- sprintf("%s: %d value(s) with codes not in the dictionary (%s)",
                   v, sum(unknown), paste(sort(unique(x[unknown])), collapse = ","))
    if (on_unknown == "error") stop(msg, call. = FALSE)
    warning(msg, call. = FALSE)
  }
  out <- rep(NA_character_, length(x))
  for (g in names(e$groups)) out[x %in% e$groups[[g]]] <- g
  # A skip label may name an existing category (the skip implies the
  # answer) or a separate "not asked" category.
  skipped <- is.na(x) & !is.null(e$skip)
  if (any(skipped)) out[skipped] <- e$skip
  out[is.na(out)] <- e$nonresponse
  levels <- unique(c(e$ref, setdiff(names(e$groups), e$ref), e$skip,
                     if (e$nonresponse == "Missing") "Missing"))
  factor(out, levels = levels)
}

code_items <- function(raw, vars, on_unknown = "error") {
  as.data.frame(lapply(setNames(vars, vars), function(v) {
    code_item(raw[[v]], coding_dictionary[[v]], v, on_unknown)
  }), stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
}

# Every recode applied to a dataset: several NHIS codes combined into one
# category, nonresponse assigned to a category, and codes not in the
# dictionary (treated as nonresponse).
describe_recodes <- function(raw, vars) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(vars, function(v) {
    e <- coding_dictionary[[v]]
    x <- raw[[v]]
    rows <- list()
    for (g in names(e$groups)) {
      codes <- e$groups[[g]]
      if (length(codes) > 1 && e$type != "continuous") {
        n <- vapply(codes, function(cd) sum(x %in% cd), integer(1))
        rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
          variable = v, action = "combined", codes = paste(codes, collapse = ","),
          n = paste(n, collapse = "/"), coded_as = g)
      }
    }
    unknown <- !is.na(x) & !(x %in% c(dictionary_codes(e), e$missing))
    if (any(unknown)) {
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        variable = v, action = "code not in dictionary",
        codes = paste(sort(unique(x[unknown])), collapse = ","),
        n = as.character(sum(unknown)), coded_as = e$nonresponse)
    }
    coded_nonresp <- x %in% e$missing
    if (any(coded_nonresp)) {
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        variable = v, action = "nonresponse code",
        codes = paste(sort(unique(x[coded_nonresp])), collapse = ","),
        n = as.character(sum(coded_nonresp)), coded_as = e$nonresponse)
    }
    blank_no_rule <- is.na(x) & is.null(e$skip)
    if (any(blank_no_rule)) {
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        variable = v, action = "blank, no skip rule", codes = "blank",
        n = as.character(sum(blank_no_rule)), coded_as = e$nonresponse)
    }
    blank_skip <- is.na(x) & !is.null(e$skip)
    if (any(blank_skip)) {
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        variable = v, action = "blank, skip rule", codes = "blank",
        n = as.character(sum(blank_skip)), coded_as = e$skip)
    }
    do.call(rbind, rows)
  }))
}
```

## 2024 sample, missingness and split

```{r prepare-2024}
nhis_2024 <- read.csv("adult24.csv")
model_data <- prepare_nhis(nhis_2024)

print(c(raw_n = nrow(nhis_2024), valid_outcome_n = nrow(model_data)))

has_complete <- complete.cases(model_data[expanded_predictors])
sample_check <- table(
  sample = ifelse(has_complete, "Retained", "Excluded"),
  telehealth = model_data$telehealth
)
print(sample_check)
print(round(100 * prop.table(sample_check, margin = 1), 1))

analysis_data <- model_data[has_complete, ]
print(c(complete_case_n = nrow(analysis_data)))

set.seed(2026)
rows_by_outcome <- split(seq_len(nrow(analysis_data)), analysis_data$telehealth)
train_rows <- sort(unlist(lapply(rows_by_outcome, function(rows) {
  sample(rows, size = floor(0.80 * length(rows)))
}), use.names = FALSE))
train_data <- analysis_data[train_rows, ]
test_data <- analysis_data[-train_rows, ]

print(data.frame(
  dataset = c("Training", "Test"),
  n = c(nrow(train_data), nrow(test_data)),
  users = c(sum(train_data$telehealth), sum(test_data$telehealth)),
  use_pct = round(100 * c(mean(train_data$telehealth),
                          mean(test_data$telehealth)), 2)
))

# Stratified 5-fold CV assignment within the training set.
k <- 5L
set.seed(2026)
fold_id <- integer(nrow(train_data))
for (rows in split(seq_len(nrow(train_data)), train_data$telehealth)) {
  fold_id[sample(rows)] <- rep(seq_len(k), length.out = length(rows))
}
validation_folds <- lapply(seq_len(k), function(f) which(fold_id == f))
```

## Screening result

Coverage is computed from the predictor values of the 2024 *training*
respondents; the only 2025 information used is the list of variable names
(whether an item was fielded in 2025). The screen never uses the outcome
or any 2025 values. The full table is written to `variable_screening.csv`.

```{r screen-items}
# Header row only: the list of items fielded in 2025.
names_2025 <- names(read.csv("adult25.csv", nrows = 0))

screening <- screen_variables(nhis_2024[train_data$source_row, ], names_2025)
write.csv(dictionary_table(), "coding_dictionary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
print(as.data.frame(table(decision = screening$decision)), row.names = FALSE)

# Candidate items beyond the theory-based set, and uncertain items that go
# through the outcome-proxy diagnostic below. Every screened item, uncertain
# ones included, is coded so that the diagnostic can use it.
new_candidates <- screening$variable[screening$decision == "Candidate: new"]
uncertain_items <- screening$variable[
  screening$decision == "Uncertain: outcome-proxy check"
]
pool_items <- c(theory_dictionary_raw, new_candidates, uncertain_items)
stopifnot(all(pool_items %in% names(coding_dictionary)))
cat("New candidates:", length(new_candidates),
    "| uncertain items to check:", length(uncertain_items), "\n")

# Theory-based items are kept regardless of coverage; report any below the
# 90% threshold that applies to the other items.
theory_rows <- screening[screening$decision == "Candidate: theory-based set", ]
cat("Theory-based items with 2024 coverage < 90%:",
    if (any(theory_rows$coverage_2024 < 0.9)) {
      paste(theory_rows$variable[theory_rows$coverage_2024 < 0.9], collapse = ", ")
    } else "none", "\n")

# Items whose coverage is not dictionary-based and whose blanks alone would
# not exclude them: their exclusion rests on the reserve-code convention.
approximate <- screening[screening$coverage_basis != "dictionary" &
                           screening$share_nonblank_2024 >= 0.9 &
                           screening$decision ==
                             "Excluded: 2024 coverage < 90% (skip pattern)", ]
cat("Exclusions resting on approximate coverage:",
    if (nrow(approximate)) paste(approximate$variable, collapse = ", ") else "none",
    "\n")

add_pool <- function(data, raw, on_unknown = "error") {
  cbind(data, code_items(raw[data$source_row, ], pool_items, on_unknown))
}
train_data <- add_pool(train_data, nhis_2024)
test_data <- add_pool(test_data, nhis_2024)

# Smallest category of each item in the training data.
smallest <- sort(vapply(train_data[pool_items], function(f) min(table(f)),
                        integer(1)))
print(head(smallest, 8))
```

The coding is fixed by the dictionary rather than learned from the data,
so it is identical inside every cross-validation fold and in 2025. Several
NHIS codes are combined into one category where categories are small or
equivalent (for example "cannot do at all" with "a lot of difficulty";
Medicare "yes, no detail" with "yes"). Nonresponse is handled per item as
written in the dictionary: a separate "Missing" category when it is about
1% or more of respondents, otherwise assignment to the most common
category. Blanks are interpreted as "not asked" only where the dictionary
gives a skip rule; other blanks are counted as nonresponse and reported
separately below. A code that the dictionary does not list stops the
analysis in 2024 and triggers a warning in 2025. Every recode in the
training data:

```{r recodes-2024}
print(describe_recodes(nhis_2024[train_data$source_row, ], pool_items),
      row.names = FALSE)
```

# Model development (training set only)

## Metrics

```{r metric-functions}
log_loss <- function(y, p) {
  p <- pmin(pmax(p, 1e-15), 1 - 1e-15)
  -mean(y * log(p) + (1 - y) * log1p(-p))
}

# Mann-Whitney AUROC; tied scores receive average ranks.
auroc <- function(p, y) {
  n1 <- sum(y == 1)
  n0 <- sum(y == 0)
  (sum(rank(p)[y == 1]) - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2) / (n1 * n0)
}

evaluate_prob <- function(prob, y) {
  auprc <- if (length(unique(prob)) == 1L) {
    mean(y)
  } else {
    pr.curve(scores.class0 = prob[y == 1],
             scores.class1 = prob[y == 0])$auc.integral
  }
  c(log_loss = log_loss(y, prob), AUROC = auroc(prob, y),
    AUPRC = auprc, Brier = mean((y - prob)^2))
}

# Calibration-in-the-large (intercept with slope fixed at 1) and slope.
calibration_stats <- function(prob, y) {
  lp <- qlogis(pmin(pmax(prob, 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6))
  c(
    mean_predicted = mean(prob),
    mean_observed = mean(y),
    cal_intercept = unname(coef(glm(y ~ offset(lp), family = binomial()))[1]),
    cal_slope = unname(coef(glm(y ~ lp, family = binomial()))[2])
  )
}

# Stop on non-convergence, aliased coefficients or non-finite predictions.
# A factor level absent from a fold's training part makes predict() stop
# with a "new levels" error, which is also surfaced rather than ignored.
check_fit <- function(fit, label) {
  if (!fit$converged) stop(label, ": glm did not converge", call. = FALSE)
  if (anyNA(coef(fit))) {
    stop(label, ": aliased coefficients ",
         paste(names(which(is.na(coef(fit)))), collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  invisible(fit)
}

cv_logistic <- function(formula) {
  vapply(seq_len(k), function(fold) {
    fit <- glm(formula, data = train_data[fold_id != fold, ],
               family = binomial())
    check_fit(fit, paste("fold", fold))
    valid <- train_data[fold_id == fold, ]
    p <- predict(fit, newdata = valid, type = "response")
    stopifnot(all(is.finite(p)))
    log_loss(valid$telehealth, p)
  }, numeric(1))
}
```

## Candidate model formulas

```{r formulas}
# The theory-based (Andersen) set: 22 items, including the five covariates
# used in the project dashboard's association model and urban-rural
# classification. None of them has a special status: in every selection
# procedure below they are candidates like any other item.
andersen_terms <- c("ns(age, df = 3)", "insurance", "education", "internet",
                    "health", setdiff(added_predictors, "pov_ratio"),
                    "ns(pov_ratio, df = 3)", theory_dictionary_raw)
f_null <- telehealth ~ 1
f_theory <- reformulate(andersen_terms, response = "telehealth")
```

## Outcome-proxy diagnostic for uncertain items

Items that a telehealth visit cannot produce, but that may act as proxies
for the outcome (in-person care use, online health activity, treatment,
prevention, cost barriers, COVID-19 history), are checked on the training
data. Each item is added to the theory-based model, and its contribution is
compared with that of the strongest theory-based predictor:

* gain in 5-fold CV log loss when the item is added, against the largest
  increase in CV log loss when one theory-based item is removed;
* likelihood-ratio statistic per degree of freedom, against the largest
  such statistic among theory-based items.

An item that exceeds either benchmark contributes more than any accepted
predictor and is excluded as a possible proxy for the outcome. Unflagged
`EVERCOVD_A` remains an ordinary candidate; the other unflagged items
describe care use or access and are used only in the borderline
sensitivity analysis. The diagnostic uses training outcomes and is not
repeated inside the nested cross-validation folds; it can show that an item
is suspicious but cannot prove that it is safe.

```{r outcome-proxy-check, cache=TRUE}
fit_terms <- function(terms_) {
  glm(reformulate(terms_, response = "telehealth"), data = train_data,
      family = binomial())
}
lr_per_df <- function(terms_full, term) {
  full <- fit_terms(terms_full)
  reduced <- fit_terms(setdiff(terms_full, term))
  (reduced$deviance - full$deviance) / (length(coef(full)) - length(coef(reduced)))
}

theory_cv <- mean(cv_logistic(f_theory))
benchmark <- data.frame(
  term = andersen_terms,
  cv_logloss_change = vapply(andersen_terms, function(t) {
    mean(cv_logistic(reformulate(setdiff(andersen_terms, t), response = "telehealth"))) -
      theory_cv
  }, numeric(1)),
  lr_per_df = vapply(andersen_terms, lr_per_df, numeric(1),
                     terms_full = andersen_terms)
)
gain_threshold <- max(benchmark$cv_logloss_change)
lr_threshold <- max(benchmark$lr_per_df)
cat("Benchmarks: CV log loss", round(gain_threshold, 5),
    "| LR per df", round(lr_threshold, 1), "\n")

check_items <- intersect(uncertain_raw, pool_items)
proxy_check <- data.frame(
  item = check_items,
  label = unname(variable_labels[check_items]),
  cv_logloss_gain = vapply(check_items, function(v) {
    theory_cv - mean(cv_logistic(reformulate(c(andersen_terms, v),
                                             response = "telehealth")))
  }, numeric(1)),
  lr_per_df = vapply(check_items, function(v) {
    lr_per_df(c(andersen_terms, v), v)
  }, numeric(1))
)
proxy_check$flagged <- proxy_check$cv_logloss_gain > gain_threshold |
  proxy_check$lr_per_df > lr_threshold
proxy_check <- proxy_check[order(-proxy_check$cv_logloss_gain), ]
print(transform(proxy_check, cv_logloss_gain = round(cv_logloss_gain, 5),
                lr_per_df = round(lr_per_df, 1)), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r candidate-pool}
flagged_items <- proxy_check$item[proxy_check$flagged]
passed_items <- proxy_check$item[!proxy_check$flagged]

new_candidates <- setdiff(new_candidates, flagged_items)
borderline_candidates <- setdiff(passed_items, uncertain_candidate_raw)

screening$decision[screening$variable %in% flagged_items] <-
  "Excluded: outcome-proxy diagnostic"
screening$decision[screening$variable %in% borderline_candidates] <-
  "Candidate: borderline (sensitivity only)"
write.csv(screening, "variable_screening.csv", row.names = FALSE)

cat("Excluded by the diagnostic:",
    if (length(flagged_items)) paste(flagged_items, collapse = ", ") else "none", "\n")
cat("Borderline (sensitivity only):", paste(borderline_candidates, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# All candidates: the theory-based set plus the screened new items.
pool_terms <- c(andersen_terms, new_candidates)
f_pool <- reformulate(pool_terms, response = "telehealth")
cat("Candidate terms:", length(pool_terms), "\n")

# No candidate may be an exact linear combination of others (for example, a
# "not asked" category identical to a category of another item): the full
# pool, with and without borderline items, must have no aliased terms.
for (f in list(f_pool, update(f_pool, paste(". ~ . +",
                                             paste(borderline_candidates,
                                                   collapse = " + "))))) {
  aliased <- names(which(is.na(coef(glm(f, data = train_data, family = binomial())))))
  if (length(aliased)) stop("Aliased coefficients: ", paste(aliased, collapse = ", "))
}
```

## Stepwise selection by BIC (primary)

Bidirectional stepwise search starting from the intercept-only model, with
every candidate (theory-based items included) free to enter or leave. The BIC
penalty is log(n) per parameter, with each item entering or leaving as a
whole (all of its levels together). This main-effects model was fixed as
the primary model before any evaluation, as a compromise between
parsimony and predictive performance rather than as the best-predicting
model. BIC does not directly optimize out-of-sample log loss, and the
stepwise search returns a good model along its path, not a guaranteed
global optimum.

```{r stepwise-bic, cache=TRUE}
n_train <- nrow(train_data)
fit_null <- glm(f_null, data = train_data, family = binomial())
fit_bic <- step(fit_null, scope = list(lower = f_null, upper = f_pool),
                direction = "both", k = log(n_train), trace = 0)

bic_terms <- attr(terms(fit_bic), "term.labels")
f_bic <- reformulate(bic_terms, response = "telehealth")

cat("Selected", length(bic_terms), "terms:\n")
print(data.frame(
  order = seq_along(bic_terms),
  term = bic_terms,
  label = ifelse(bic_terms %in% names(variable_labels),
                 variable_labels[bic_terms], "(theory-based set)")
), row.names = FALSE)

# Were the five dashboard covariates selected without being forced in?
dashboard_terms <- c("ns(age, df = 3)", "insurance", "education", "internet", "health")
print(data.frame(term = dashboard_terms, selected = dashboard_terms %in% bic_terms),
      row.names = FALSE)
```

## Stepwise BIC within the theory-based items

The same search restricted to the 22 theory-based (Andersen) items. Compared
with the full theory-based model, it shows whether that set can be
simplified; compared with the primary model, it isolates the contribution
of the wider candidate pool.

```{r stepwise-bic-theory, cache=TRUE}
fit_bic_theory <- step(fit_null, scope = list(lower = f_null, upper = f_theory),
                       direction = "both", k = log(n_train), trace = 0)
bic_theory_terms <- attr(terms(fit_bic_theory), "term.labels")
f_bic_theory <- reformulate(bic_theory_terms, response = "telehealth")

cat("Kept", length(bic_theory_terms), "of", length(andersen_terms),
    "theory-based terms:", paste(bic_theory_terms, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Dropped:", paste(setdiff(andersen_terms, bic_theory_terms), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## Group lasso (cross-check)

Each item is one group (all of its dummy columns or spline bases), and
every group is penalized. The penalty is tuned with the same 5 folds. Both
the lambda.min fit and the sparser 1-SE fit are carried forward to the
test-set and 2025 comparisons.

```{r group-lasso, cache=TRUE}
# Build the design from a given set of rows. The terms object carries the
# spline knots of those rows ("predvars"), so any other data get the same
# basis.
build_design <- function(fit_data) {
  terms_object <- terms(model.frame(reformulate(pool_terms), data = fit_data))
  mm <- model.matrix(terms_object, model.frame(terms_object, data = fit_data))
  term_of_column <- attr(terms_object, "term.labels")[attr(mm, "assign")[-1]]
  group_id <- as.integer(factor(term_of_column, levels = unique(term_of_column)))
  list(
    x = mm[, -1, drop = FALSE], term_of_column = term_of_column,
    group_id = group_id,
    matrix_for = function(data) {
      model.matrix(terms_object, model.frame(terms_object, data = data))[, -1, drop = FALSE]
    }
  )
}

train_design <- build_design(train_data)
x_train <- train_design$x
term_of_column <- train_design$term_of_column
group_id <- train_design$group_id
design_matrix <- train_design$matrix_for

set.seed(2026)
cv_glasso <- cv.grpreg(x_train, train_data$telehealth, group = group_id,
                       penalty = "grLasso", family = "binomial",
                       fold = fold_id, nlambda = 60)

i_min <- which.min(cv_glasso$cve)
i_1se <- min(which(cv_glasso$cve <= cv_glasso$cve[i_min] + cv_glasso$cvse[i_min]))

selected_groups <- function(i) {
  b <- cv_glasso$fit$beta[-1, i]
  unique(term_of_column[b != 0])
}
glasso_min_terms <- selected_groups(i_min)
glasso_1se_terms <- selected_groups(i_1se)

print(data.frame(
  rule = c("lambda.min", "lambda.1se"),
  lambda = signif(cv_glasso$lambda[c(i_min, i_1se)], 3),
  cv_logloss = round(cv_glasso$cve[c(i_min, i_1se)] / 2, 5),
  n_terms = c(length(glasso_min_terms), length(glasso_1se_terms))
), row.names = FALSE)

cat("BIC terms not kept by group lasso (1se):",
    setdiff(bic_terms, glasso_1se_terms), "\n")
```

## Selection stability

Two separate questions. (1) *Is the BIC selection itself stable?* Stepwise
BIC is rerun on 20 random half-samples of the training set. (2) *Which items
does a different method favour?* Group lasso at the 1-SE penalty is refit on
50 half-samples. The frequencies are descriptive; disagreement between the
two methods reflects their different penalties and is not evidence that
either is wrong.

```{r bic-half-sample, cache=TRUE}
run_parallel <- function(x, fun) {
  if (.Platform$OS.type == "unix") {
    check_workers(mclapply(x, fun, mc.cores = n_workers))
  } else {
    lapply(x, fun)
  }
}

n_bic_subsamples <- 20L
set.seed(2026)
bic_subsample_rows <- lapply(seq_len(n_bic_subsamples),
                             function(b) sample.int(n_train, floor(n_train / 2)))

bic_on_rows <- function(rows) {
  half <- train_data[rows, ]
  lower <- f_null
  upper <- f_pool
  # Formulas must look up `half` here, not in the global environment.
  environment(lower) <- environment(upper) <- environment()
  start <- glm(lower, data = half, family = binomial())
  fit <- step(start, scope = list(lower = lower, upper = upper),
              direction = "both", k = log(nrow(half)), trace = 0)
  attr(terms(fit), "term.labels")
}
bic_subsample_terms <- run_parallel(bic_subsample_rows, bic_on_rows)
bic_frequency <- table(factor(unlist(bic_subsample_terms), levels = pool_terms))
cat("Terms selected per half-sample:",
    paste(range(lengths(bic_subsample_terms)), collapse = " to "), "\n")
```

```{r glasso-subsampling, cache=TRUE}
set.seed(2026)
n_subsamples <- 50L
lambda_path <- cv_glasso$lambda[seq_len(i_1se)]
glasso_counts <- setNames(numeric(length(pool_terms)), pool_terms)

for (b in seq_len(n_subsamples)) {
  rows <- sample.int(n_train, floor(n_train / 2))
  fit <- grpreg(x_train[rows, ], train_data$telehealth[rows], group = group_id,
                penalty = "grLasso", family = "binomial", lambda = lambda_path)
  beta <- fit$beta[-1, ncol(fit$beta)]
  chosen <- unique(term_of_column[beta != 0])
  glasso_counts[chosen] <- glasso_counts[chosen] + 1
}

selection_frequency <- data.frame(
  term = pool_terms,
  label = ifelse(pool_terms %in% names(variable_labels),
                 variable_labels[pool_terms], "(theory-based set)"),
  in_primary_model = pool_terms %in% bic_terms,
  bic_half_sample_pct = round(100 * as.numeric(bic_frequency[pool_terms]) /
                                n_bic_subsamples),
  glasso_half_sample_pct = round(100 * glasso_counts / n_subsamples)
)
selection_frequency <- selection_frequency[
  order(-selection_frequency$bic_half_sample_pct,
        -selection_frequency$glasso_half_sample_pct), ]
print(head(selection_frequency, 35), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Gradient boosting (XGBoost)

Tuned on the full candidate pool, as a reference for what a flexible
method can extract from the screened items. The tuning scores below come from the
same folds used to choose depth, learning rate and number of rounds, so
they are not unbiased performance estimates.

```{r xgboost-cv, cache=TRUE}
xgb_matrix <- function(data, vars) {
  x <- model.matrix(reformulate(vars), data = data)
  x[, colnames(x) != "(Intercept)", drop = FALSE]
}

xgb_grid <- expand.grid(max_depth = 1:3, eta = c(0.05, 0.10))
max_rounds <- 8000L

tune_xgb <- function(vars) {
  x <- xgb_matrix(train_data, vars)
  dtrain <- xgb.DMatrix(x, label = train_data$telehealth)
  results <- xgb_grid
  results$best_nrounds <- NA_integer_
  results$cv_logloss <- NA_real_

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(results))) {
    params <- list(
      objective = "binary:logistic", eval_metric = "logloss",
      tree_method = "hist", max_depth = results$max_depth[i],
      eta = results$eta[i], min_child_weight = 10
    )
    cv <- xgb.cv(params = params, data = dtrain, folds = validation_folds,
                 nrounds = max_rounds, early_stopping_rounds = 50, verbose = 0)
    loss <- cv$evaluation_log$test_logloss_mean
    results$best_nrounds[i] <- which.min(loss)
    results$cv_logloss[i] <- min(loss)
  }

  stopifnot(all(results$best_nrounds < max_rounds))
  best <- results[which.min(results$cv_logloss), ]
  params <- list(
    objective = "binary:logistic", eval_metric = "logloss",
    tree_method = "hist", max_depth = best$max_depth, eta = best$eta,
    min_child_weight = 10
  )
  list(grid = results[order(results$cv_logloss), ], params = params,
       nrounds = best$best_nrounds, vars = vars)
}

pool_vars <- c(expanded_predictors, theory_dictionary_raw, new_candidates)

set.seed(2026)
xgb_pool <- tune_xgb(pool_vars)
print(xgb_pool$grid, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Nested cross-validation of the selection procedures

Cross-validating a final selected formula, or a group-lasso fit whose
penalty was tuned on the same folds, does not account for the selection
step. Here each whole procedure is repeated inside each outer fold, using
only the other four folds: stepwise BIC (on the full pool and on the
theory-based items) is rerun, and for group lasso the spline basis is
rebuilt and the penalty is tuned by an inner 5-fold CV. The held-out fold
is used only for scoring. This evaluates the selection and fitting steps
*given the screened candidate set*: screening and dictionary coding are
done once beforehand and are not repeated inside folds, and the inner CV
of group lasso uses the spline basis of the outer training part. It is
therefore not an evaluation of the complete pipeline from the raw file.

```{r nested-cv, cache=TRUE}
run_folds <- function(fun) {
  if (.Platform$OS.type == "unix") {
    check_workers(mclapply(seq_len(k), fun, mc.cores = min(k, n_workers)))
  } else {
    lapply(seq_len(k), fun)
  }
}

nested_bic_fold <- function(fold, upper_formula) {
  inner <- train_data[fold_id != fold, ]
  outer <- train_data[fold_id == fold, ]
  lower <- f_null
  upper <- upper_formula
  # Formulas must look up `inner` here, not in the global environment.
  environment(lower) <- environment(upper) <- environment()
  start <- glm(lower, data = inner, family = binomial())
  fit <- step(start, scope = list(lower = lower, upper = upper),
              direction = "both", k = log(nrow(inner)), trace = 0)
  check_fit(fit, paste("nested BIC, fold", fold))
  p <- predict(fit, newdata = outer, type = "response")
  stopifnot(all(is.finite(p)))
  list(loss = log_loss(outer$telehealth, p),
       terms = attr(terms(fit), "term.labels"))
}

nested_glasso_fold <- function(fold) {
  inner <- train_data[fold_id != fold, ]
  outer <- train_data[fold_id == fold, ]
  design <- build_design(inner)
  set.seed(2026 + fold)
  inner_fold <- integer(nrow(inner))
  for (rows in split(seq_len(nrow(inner)), inner$telehealth)) {
    inner_fold[sample(rows)] <- rep(seq_len(k), length.out = length(rows))
  }
  cv_in <- cv.grpreg(design$x, inner$telehealth, group = design$group_id,
                     penalty = "grLasso", family = "binomial",
                     fold = inner_fold, nlambda = 60)
  j_min <- which.min(cv_in$cve)
  j_1se <- min(which(cv_in$cve <= cv_in$cve[j_min] + cv_in$cvse[j_min]))
  x_out <- design$matrix_for(outer)
  score <- function(j) {
    log_loss(outer$telehealth,
             as.numeric(predict(cv_in$fit, x_out, lambda = cv_in$lambda[j],
                                type = "response")))
  }
  c(lambda_min = score(j_min), lambda_1se = score(j_1se))
}

nested_bic <- run_folds(function(f) nested_bic_fold(f, f_pool))
nested_bic_theory <- run_folds(function(f) nested_bic_fold(f, f_theory))
nested_glasso <- do.call(rbind, run_folds(nested_glasso_fold))

nested_bic_loss <- vapply(nested_bic, `[[`, numeric(1), "loss")
nested_bic_theory_loss <- vapply(nested_bic_theory, `[[`, numeric(1), "loss")
print(round(data.frame(
  fold = seq_len(k),
  stepwise_BIC_pool = nested_bic_loss,
  stepwise_BIC_theory = nested_bic_theory_loss,
  group_lasso_min = nested_glasso[, "lambda_min"],
  group_lasso_1se = nested_glasso[, "lambda_1se"]
), 5), row.names = FALSE)

# How often each term is reselected by stepwise BIC (full pool) across
# outer folds.
all_selected <- unlist(lapply(nested_bic, `[[`, "terms"))
reselected <- table(factor(all_selected, levels = union(bic_terms, all_selected)))
print(data.frame(term = names(reselected),
                 folds_selected = as.integer(reselected),
                 in_primary_model = names(reselected) %in% bic_terms),
      row.names = FALSE)
```

## Comparison of cross-validated performance

For the selection procedures, the nested estimates are the ones to
compare. XGBoost was tuned on the same folds used to score it, so its
tuning scores are shown in a separate column and are not ranked against
the other models. The 2024 test set gives the final comparison of all
models, including XGBoost.

```{r cv-comparison, cache=TRUE}
cv_table <- data.frame(
  model = c("Theory-based, all 22 items", "Theory-based, stepwise BIC",
            "Full screened pool, no selection", "Stepwise BIC, full pool (primary)",
            "Group lasso, lambda.min", "Group lasso, lambda.1se",
            "Full pool, XGBoost"),
  n_terms = c(length(andersen_terms), length(bic_theory_terms), length(pool_terms),
              length(bic_terms), length(glasso_min_terms),
              length(glasso_1se_terms), length(pool_terms)),
  cv_logloss = c(
    mean(cv_logistic(f_theory)), mean(nested_bic_theory_loss),
    mean(cv_logistic(f_pool)), mean(nested_bic_loss),
    mean(nested_glasso[, "lambda_min"]), mean(nested_glasso[, "lambda_1se"]),
    NA_real_
  ),
  # Not comparable with the column above: tuned and scored on the same folds.
  xgb_tuning_score = c(rep(NA_real_, 6), min(xgb_pool$grid$cv_logloss)),
  estimate = c("standard CV", "nested CV", "standard CV", "nested CV",
               "nested CV", "nested CV", "tuning score (not ranked)")
)
cv_table$cv_logloss <- round(cv_table$cv_logloss, 5)
cv_table$xgb_tuning_score <- round(cv_table$xgb_tuning_score, 5)
print(cv_table, row.names = FALSE)

cat("Apparent CV log loss of the final BIC formula (selection not repeated):",
    round(mean(cv_logistic(f_bic)), 5), "| nested:", round(mean(nested_bic_loss), 5),
    "\n")
```

## Sensitivity: borderline items

Starting from the BIC model, borderline items (uncertain items that
passed the outcome-proxy diagnostic but describe care use or access) are
offered for forward entry under the same BIC criterion. This analysis is exploratory:
the items are selected on the full training set and then cross-validated
as a fixed formula, so the reported CV log loss is an *apparent* value,
not comparable with the nested estimates above. It does not change the
primary model.

```{r borderline-sensitivity, cache=TRUE}
f_bic_border_upper <- reformulate(c(bic_terms, borderline_candidates),
                                  response = "telehealth")
fit_border <- step(fit_bic, scope = list(lower = f_bic, upper = f_bic_border_upper),
                   direction = "forward", k = log(n_train), trace = 0)
border_added <- setdiff(attr(terms(fit_border), "term.labels"),
                        bic_terms)
cat("Borderline items entering:",
    if (length(border_added)) paste(border_added, collapse = ", ") else "none", "\n")
if (length(border_added)) {
  print(round(c(
    apparent_cv_logloss_bic = mean(cv_logistic(f_bic)),
    apparent_cv_logloss_bic_plus_borderline = mean(cv_logistic(formula(fit_border)))
  ), 5))
}
```

Survey-weighted versions of the same metrics describe performance for the
population represented by the complete-case test respondents (weights are
the original NHIS adult weights; complete-case exclusion is not
reweighted).

```{r weighted-metrics-function}
# Weighted Mann-Whitney AUROC: sum over positive-negative pairs of
# w_i * w_j * [p_i > p_j] (ties count one half), divided by the product of
# the positive and negative weight totals.
weighted_auroc <- function(p, y, w) {
  g <- match(p, sort(unique(p)))
  w_pos <- tapply(w * (y == 1), g, sum)
  w_neg <- tapply(w * (y == 0), g, sum)
  below <- cumsum(w_neg) - w_neg
  sum(w_pos * (below + 0.5 * w_neg)) / (sum(w_pos) * sum(w_neg))
}

weighted_metrics <- function(prob, y, w) {
  p <- pmin(pmax(prob, 1e-15), 1 - 1e-15)
  w <- w / sum(w)
  c(log_loss = -sum(w * (y * log(p) + (1 - y) * log1p(-p))),
    AUROC = weighted_auroc(prob, y, w),
    Brier = sum(w * (y - prob)^2))
}

stopifnot(abs(weighted_auroc(test_prob[[primary_model]], y_test,
                             rep(1, length(y_test))) -
                auroc(test_prob[[primary_model]], y_test)) < 1e-10)

weight_test <- test_data$survey_weight
print(round(t(vapply(test_prob, weighted_metrics, numeric(3),
                     y = y_test, w = weight_test)), 4))
```

## Bootstrap confidence intervals

Paired bootstrap with 1,000 replicates. Within each NHIS stratum,
primary sampling units (PSUs) are drawn with replacement and all of their
sampled respondents are kept, so the intervals account for stratified
cluster sampling. They apply to the *unweighted* metrics of models that are
already fitted: they do not include uncertainty from training or variable
selection, and they are not a full design-based inference for weighted
metrics (which would use replicate weights or linearization). Gains are
positive when the primary model is better.

```{r bootstrap-function}
# Row indices grouped by PSU within stratum.
psu_index <- function(data) {
  key <- paste(data$survey_stratum, data$survey_psu)
  rows_by_psu <- split(seq_len(nrow(data)), key)
  stratum_of_psu <- sub(" .*", "", names(rows_by_psu))
  split(rows_by_psu, stratum_of_psu)
}

draw_psu_sample <- function(index) {
  unlist(lapply(index, function(psus) {
    psus[sample.int(length(psus), length(psus), replace = TRUE)]
  }), use.names = FALSE)
}

bootstrap_compare <- function(prob, y, index, B = 1000, seed = 2026) {
  set.seed(seed)
  primary <- prob[[primary_model]]
  comparators <- c("Theory-based logistic",
                   "Theory-based BIC logistic", "Group lasso (lambda.min)",
                   "Group lasso (lambda.1se)", "Full pool XGBoost")
  draws <- replicate(B, {
    i <- draw_psu_sample(index)
    a_primary <- auroc(primary[i], y[i])
    l_primary <- log_loss(y[i], primary[i])
    c(primary_AUROC = a_primary,
      unlist(lapply(setNames(comparators, comparators), function(m) {
        c(AUROC_gain = a_primary - auroc(prob[[m]][i], y[i]),
          logloss_gain = log_loss(y[i], prob[[m]][i]) - l_primary)
      })))
  })
  t(apply(draws, 1, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)))
}

test_psu_index <- psu_index(test_data)
cat("Test set:", length(test_psu_index), "strata,",
    sum(lengths(test_psu_index)), "PSUs\n")
print(round(bootstrap_compare(test_prob, y_test, test_psu_index), 4))
```

## Calibration

```{r calibration-test}
print(round(t(vapply(test_prob[-1], calibration_stats, numeric(4),
                     y = y_test)), 4))

calibration_by_band <- function(prob, y, weight = rep(1, length(y))) {
  band <- cut(prob, breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.10), include.lowest = TRUE)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(split(seq_along(prob), band, drop = TRUE),
                        function(rows) {
    w <- weight[rows]
    data.frame(
      n = length(rows),
      weighted_share_pct = 100 * sum(w) / sum(weight),
      predicted = weighted.mean(prob[rows], w),
      observed = weighted.mean(y[rows], w),
      gap_pp = 100 * (weighted.mean(y[rows], w) - weighted.mean(prob[rows], w))
    )
  }))
}

cal_test <- calibration_by_band(test_prob[[primary_model]], y_test)
print(round(cal_test, 4))
```

Response codes in 2025 are compared with the coding dictionary. A code
that the dictionary does not list triggers a warning and is treated as
nonresponse: for screened items it receives the item's nonresponse
handling; for theory-based items it becomes missing and the
respondent drops out of the complete-case sample. Codes listed in the
dictionary but absent in 2025 are also reported.

```{r coding-check-2025}
check_coding <- function(item) {
  e <- coding_dictionary[[item]]
  x25 <- nhis_2025[[item]][valid_2025]
  observed <- x25[!is.na(x25) & !(x25 %in% e$missing)]
  if (e$type == "continuous") {
    g <- e$groups[[1]]
    outside <- observed[observed < min(g) | observed > max(g)]
    return(data.frame(
      item = item, coverage_2025 = round(item_coverage(item, x25), 3),
      not_in_dictionary = if (length(outside)) sprintf("%g to %g", min(outside),
                                                       max(outside)) else "",
      n_not_in_dictionary = length(outside), absent_in_2025 = ""))
  }
  codes <- dictionary_codes(e)
  unknown <- sort(unique(observed[!(observed %in% codes)]))
  data.frame(
    item = item, coverage_2025 = round(item_coverage(item, x25), 3),
    not_in_dictionary = paste(unknown, collapse = ","),
    n_not_in_dictionary = sum(observed %in% unknown),
    absent_in_2025 = paste(setdiff(codes, observed), collapse = ",")
  )
}

coding_check <- do.call(rbind, lapply(model_items[["Group lasso / full pool XGBoost"]],
                                      check_coding))
coding_check$in_primary_model <- coding_check$item %in%
  model_items[["Stepwise BIC logistic"]]

cat("Items with codes not in the dictionary, or dictionary codes absent in 2025:\n")

                              c("item", "label", "coverage_2025")]

      row.names = FALSE)
```

Design-based 95% CI for the weighted calibration gap (observed minus

```{r weighted-gap-ci-2025}

weighted_gap <- function(model_name) {
  nhis_2025$gap_pp <- NA_real_
  nhis_2025$gap_pp[design_rows] <- 100 * (y_2025 - prob_2025[[model_name]])
  design <- svydesign(ids = ~PPSU, strata = ~PSTRAT, weights = ~WTFA_A,
                      data = nhis_2025, nest = TRUE)

  est <- svymean(~gap_pp, domain)
  ci <- confint(est, df = degf(domain))
  c(gap_pp = unname(coef(est)), lower_95 = ci[1, 1], upper_95 = ci[1, 2])
}
```

# Sensitivity: survey-weighted model fitting

The primary formula is refit with the NHIS adult weights (rescaled to mean
1; quasibinomial family, so point estimates equal weighted maximum
likelihood). Variable selection is not repeated. Both versions are scored
unweighted and weighted in the 2024 test set and in 2025.

```{r weighted-fit}
train_w <- train_data$survey_weight / mean(train_data$survey_weight)
fit_primary_weighted <- glm(f_bic, data = train_data, family = quasibinomial(),
                            weights = train_w)

score_versions <- function(data, y, w) {
  p_unw <- unname(predict(fit_primary, data, type = "response"))
  p_w <- unname(predict(fit_primary_weighted, data, type = "response"))
  rbind(
    "Unweighted fit, unweighted metrics" = evaluate_prob(p_unw, y)[c("log_loss", "AUROC", "Brier")],
    "Weighted fit, unweighted metrics" = evaluate_prob(p_w, y)[c("log_loss", "AUROC", "Brier")],
    "Unweighted fit, weighted metrics" = weighted_metrics(p_unw, y, w),
    "Weighted fit, weighted metrics" = weighted_metrics(p_w, y, w)
  )
}
```
