# Sensitivity: collinearity and interactions

## Collinearity

Generalized variance inflation factors (Fox and Monette), computed from the
correlation of the coefficient estimates as in `car::vif()`. For an item
with df parameters, GVIF^(1/(2·df)) is comparable to the square root of a
classic VIF; values above about 2.2 (VIF > 5) deserve attention.

```{r collinearity-gvif}
gvif_table <- function(fit) {
  R <- cov2cor(vcov(fit)[-1, -1])
  assign <- attr(model.matrix(fit), "assign")[-1]
  labels <- attr(terms(fit), "term.labels")
  det_R <- det(R)
  out <- t(vapply(seq_along(labels), function(j) {
    idx <- which(assign == j)
    g <- det(R[idx, idx, drop = FALSE]) * det(R[-idx, -idx, drop = FALSE]) / det_R
    c(df = length(idx), GVIF = g, GVIF_adjusted = g^(1 / (2 * length(idx))))
  }, numeric(3)))
  out <- data.frame(term = labels, round(out, 3))
  out[order(-out$GVIF_adjusted), ]
}

cat("Primary (stepwise BIC) model\n")
print(head(gvif_table(fit_primary), 10), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nTheory-based (Andersen) model\n")
print(head(gvif_table(fit_theory), 10), row.names = FALSE)
```

Several items with large raw GVIFs have a Missing/Unknown category. One
possible explanation is that largely the same respondents (about 3%) are
unascertained on several of these items; the cross-tabulation below checks
how much these categories overlap. This is a diagnostic, not a proof of
the source of the inflation.

```{r missing-overlap}
# Respondents in the Missing/Unknown category of at least one item, and of
# every item, in each group of items with high GVIF.
missing_overlap <- function(data, items, level) {
  flags <- vapply(items, function(v) data[[v]] == level, logical(nrow(data)))
  c(any_item = sum(rowSums(flags) > 0), all_items = sum(rowSums(flags) == length(items)))
}
print(rbind(
  "Primary: voted / public meeting (Missing)" =
    missing_overlap(train_data, c("CEVOTELC_A", "CEMMETNG_A"), "Missing"),
  "Theory-based: marital / U.S.-born / worked (Unknown)" =
    missing_overlap(train_data, c("marital", "us_born", "worked_last_week"), "Unknown")
))
```

Pairwise association between the predictors of the primary model
(Cramér's V; continuous variables split into quartiles):

```{r pairwise-association}
as_categories <- function(x) {
  if (is.numeric(x)) cut(x, unique(quantile(x, 0:4 / 4)), include.lowest = TRUE) else x
}
cramers_v <- function(a, b) {
  tab <- table(as_categories(a), as_categories(b))
  chi2 <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab, correct = FALSE)$statistic)
  unname(sqrt(chi2 / (sum(tab) * (min(dim(tab)) - 1))))
}

primary_vars <- all.vars(f_bic)[-1]
var_pairs <- t(combn(primary_vars, 2))
association <- data.frame(
  var1 = var_pairs[, 1], var2 = var_pairs[, 2],
  cramers_v = round(apply(var_pairs, 1, function(p) {
    cramers_v(train_data[[p[1]]], train_data[[p[2]]])
  }), 3)
)
print(head(association[order(-association$cramers_v), ], 12), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Pairwise interactions

This analysis is exploratory. All pairwise interactions among the terms
of each model are screened in one pass (change in BIC when each is added
alone); those that lower BIC are then offered to a forward stepwise BIC
search. Selection uses the full training set, and the resulting formula is
then cross-validated, so the CV log loss is an *apparent* value that is not
comparable with the nested estimates.

```{r interaction-selection, cache=TRUE}
select_interactions <- function(fit) {
  labels <- attr(terms(fit), "term.labels")
  candidates <- apply(t(combn(labels, 2)), 1, paste, collapse = ":")
  screen <- add1(fit, scope = reformulate(c(labels, candidates)),
                 k = log(n_train))[-1, ]
  base_bic <- extractAIC(fit, k = log(n_train))[2]
  screen <- data.frame(interaction = rownames(screen), df = screen$Df,
                       delta_BIC = screen$AIC - base_bic)
  screen <- screen[order(screen$delta_BIC), ]

  passed <- screen$interaction[screen$delta_BIC < 0]
  final_formula <- formula(fit)
  if (length(passed)) {
    upper <- update(formula(fit), paste(". ~ . +", paste(passed, collapse = " + ")))
    final_fit <- step(fit, scope = list(lower = formula(fit), upper = upper),
                      direction = "forward", k = log(n_train), trace = 0)
    final_formula <- formula(final_fit)
  }
  added <- setdiff(attr(terms(final_formula), "term.labels"), labels)
  list(screen = screen, n_candidates = length(candidates),
       added = added, formula = final_formula)
}

interactions <- list(
  "Stepwise BIC" = select_interactions(fit_primary),
  "Theory-based" = select_interactions(fit_theory)
)

for (m in names(interactions)) {
  x <- interactions[[m]]
  cat("\n", m, "model:", sum(x$screen$delta_BIC < 0), "of", x$n_candidates,
      "interactions lower BIC when added alone\n")
  shown <- head(x$screen, 10)
  shown$delta_BIC <- round(shown$delta_BIC, 1)
  print(shown, row.names = FALSE)
  cat("Entered by forward BIC:",
      if (length(x$added)) paste(x$added, collapse = ", ") else "none", "\n")
}
```

```{r interaction-performance, cache=TRUE}
base_formulas <- list("Stepwise BIC" = f_bic, "Theory-based" = f_theory)

interaction_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(base_formulas), function(m) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c("Main effects", "With interactions"), function(version) {
    f <- if (version == "Main effects") base_formulas[[m]] else interactions[[m]]$formula
    fit <- glm(f, data = train_data, family = binomial())
    p_test <- predict(fit, test_data, type = "response")
    p_2025 <- predict(fit, validation_2025, type = "response")
    data.frame(
      model = m, version = version, n_parameters = length(coef(fit)),
      apparent_cv_logloss = round(mean(cv_logistic(f)), 5),
      test_logloss = round(log_loss(y_test, p_test), 4),
      test_AUROC = round(auroc(p_test, y_test), 4),
      logloss_2025 = round(log_loss(y_2025, p_2025), 4),
      AUROC_2025 = round(auroc(p_2025, y_2025), 4)
    )
  }))
}))
print(interaction_results, row.names = FALSE)
```

The primary model remains the main-effects model fixed before
evaluation; the interaction results do not change it and are not used to
choose between model structures.

# Interpretation of the primary model

Odds ratios from the stepwise BIC model (unweighted, training set). They
describe adjusted associations useful for prediction, are conditional on
the selected model (post-selection intervals are too narrow), and are not
causal effects or population estimates. The intervals ignore the survey
design and the selection step, so they should not be used to call any
predictor a significant risk factor. Category names come from the coding
dictionary.

```{r odds-ratios}
coefs <- summary(fit_primary)$coefficients
keep <- !grepl("^\\(Intercept\\)|^ns\\(", rownames(coefs))
or_table <- data.frame(
  term = rownames(coefs)[keep],
  OR = exp(coefs[keep, "Estimate"]),
  lower_95 = exp(coefs[keep, "Estimate"] - 1.96 * coefs[keep, "Std. Error"]),
  upper_95 = exp(coefs[keep, "Estimate"] + 1.96 * coefs[keep, "Std. Error"])
)
or_table$item <- vapply(or_table$term, function(t) {
  hit <- names(variable_labels)[startsWith(t, names(variable_labels))]
  if (length(hit)) variable_labels[hit[which.max(nchar(hit))]] else ""
}, character(1))
print(or_table, row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
```

The curves below are *reference-profile* predictions: predicted
probability for one hypothetical adult whose other predictors are fixed at
the most common category (or the median). They show the shape of the
spline terms; they are not population-average effects.

```{r spline-effects, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
model_vars <- all.vars(f_bic)[-1]
reference_profile <- train_data[1, model_vars]
for (v in model_vars) {
  x <- train_data[[v]]
  reference_profile[[v]] <- if (is.factor(x)) {
    factor(names(which.max(table(x))), levels = levels(x))
  } else median(x)
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
if ("age" %in% model_vars) {
  age_grid <- reference_profile[rep(1, 68), ]
  age_grid$age <- 18:85
  plot(18:85, predict(fit_primary, age_grid, type = "response"), type = "l",
       lwd = 2, col = "#B31B1B", xlab = "Age (years)",
       ylab = "Predicted probability (reference profile)", main = "Age")
}
if ("pov_ratio" %in% model_vars) {
  pov_seq <- seq(0, 11, by = 0.1)
  pov_grid <- reference_profile[rep(1, length(pov_seq)), ]
  pov_grid$pov_ratio <- pov_seq
  plot(pov_seq, predict(fit_primary, pov_grid, type = "response"), type = "l",
       lwd = 2, col = "#B31B1B", xlab = "Family income / poverty threshold",
       ylab = "Predicted probability (reference profile)",
       main = "Income-to-poverty ratio")
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r drop-one-importance, cache=TRUE}
# Increase in mean CV log loss when each item is removed from the primary
# model.
base_loss <- mean(cv_logistic(f_bic))
drop_one <- vapply(bic_terms, function(t) {
  kept <- setdiff(bic_terms, t)
  mean(cv_logistic(reformulate(kept, response = "telehealth"))) - base_loss
}, numeric(1))
importance <- data.frame(
  term = names(drop_one),
  label = ifelse(names(drop_one) %in% names(variable_labels),
                 variable_labels[names(drop_one)], ""),
  cv_logloss_increase = round(drop_one, 5)
)
print(importance[order(-importance$cv_logloss_increase), ], row.names = FALSE)
```

# Model export

The fitted models are written to `model_export/` so that they can be
reported in full (TRIPOD) and applied to new data without rerunning this
document. The logistic and group lasso models are exported as coefficient
tables, together with the spline knots and factor levels estimated from the
2024 training data; the XGBoost model is saved in xgboost's JSON format.
Full R model objects are not saved, because they contain a copy of the
training data. The standalone scoring function below reads only the
exported files; the last chunk checks that it reproduces the 2025
predictions of every exported model.

```{r model-export}
export_dir <- "model_export"
dir.create(export_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Coefficients. Column names follow R's model.matrix() naming: a factor
# level is the variable name followed by the level label, and a spline
# basis is the term followed by 1, 2, 3. The first level of each factor is
# the reference category.
logistic_fits <- list(
  "Theory-based logistic" = fit_theory,
  "Theory-based BIC logistic" = fit_theory_bic,
  "Stepwise BIC logistic" = fit_primary
)
logistic_coefficients <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(logistic_fits), function(m) {
  fit <- logistic_fits[[m]]
  stopifnot(!anyNA(coef(fit)))
  assign_ <- attr(model.matrix(fit), "assign")
  data.frame(
    model = m,
    term = c("(Intercept)", attr(terms(fit), "term.labels"))[assign_ + 1],
    column = names(coef(fit)),
    estimate = unname(coef(fit)),
    std_error = unname(sqrt(diag(vcov(fit))))
  )
}))

# Group lasso: penalized estimates on the original scale, nonzero groups
# only. No standard errors are defined for these estimates.
glasso_coefficients <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  list("Group lasso (lambda.min)" = i_min, "Group lasso (lambda.1se)" = i_1se),
  function(i) {
    b <- coef(cv_glasso$fit, lambda = cv_glasso$lambda[i])
    stopifnot(identical(names(b)[-1], colnames(x_train)))
    keep <- c(TRUE, b[-1] != 0)
    data.frame(
      term = c("(Intercept)", term_of_column)[keep],
      column = names(b)[keep],
      estimate = unname(b[keep]),
      std_error = NA_real_
    )
  }))
glasso_coefficients$model <- sub("\\.[0-9]+$", "", rownames(glasso_coefficients))
glasso_coefficients <- glasso_coefficients[, names(logistic_coefficients)]

model_coefficients <- rbind(logistic_coefficients, glasso_coefficients)
rownames(model_coefficients) <- NULL
write.csv(model_coefficients, file.path(export_dir, "model_coefficients.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

# Spline knots (quantiles of the 2024 training data). All models were fit to
# the same rows, so they share one set of knots.
spline_knots <- function(fit) {
  calls <- as.list(attr(terms(fit), "predvars"))[-1]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(calls, function(e) {
    if (!is.call(e) || !deparse(e[[1]]) %in% c("ns", "splines::ns")) return(NULL)
    v <- deparse(e[[2]])
    rbind(data.frame(variable = v, type = "interior", value = unname(eval(e$knots))),
          data.frame(variable = v, type = "boundary",
                     value = unname(eval(e$Boundary.knots))))
  }))
}
knots_table <- spline_knots(fit_theory)
sort_knots <- function(k) k[order(k$variable, k$type, k$value), "value"]
for (fit in logistic_fits) {
  k <- spline_knots(fit)
  stopifnot(identical(sort_knots(k),
                      sort_knots(knots_table[knots_table$variable %in% k$variable, ])))
}
write.csv(knots_table, file.path(export_dir, "spline_knots.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
print(knots_table, row.names = FALSE)

# Factor levels, in model order (the first level is the reference).
model_vars_all <- unique(sub("^ns\\(([^,]+),.*$", "\\1",
                             setdiff(model_coefficients$term, "(Intercept)")))
factor_vars <- model_vars_all[vapply(model_vars_all,
                                     function(v) is.factor(train_data[[v]]),
                                     logical(1))]
for (m in names(logistic_fits)) {
  xl <- logistic_fits[[m]]$xlevels
  for (v in names(xl)) stopifnot(identical(xl[[v]], levels(train_data[[v]])))
}
factor_levels <- do.call(rbind, lapply(factor_vars, function(v) {
  lev <- levels(train_data[[v]])
  data.frame(variable = v, level_order = seq_along(lev), level = lev,
             reference = seq_along(lev) == 1)
}))
write.csv(factor_levels, file.path(export_dir, "factor_levels.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# XGBoost: model file, input columns and tuning result.
invisible(xgb.save(xgb_pool_fit, file.path(export_dir, "xgb_full_pool.json")))
write.csv(data.frame(feature = colnames(xgb_matrix(train_data, pool_vars))),
          file.path(export_dir, "xgb_features.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(data.frame(setting = c(names(xgb_pool$params), "nrounds"),
                     value = c(vapply(xgb_pool$params, as.character, ""),
                               as.character(xgb_pool$nrounds))),
          file.path(export_dir, "xgb_settings.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Coding rules needed to prepare the raw NHIS items.
invisible(file.copy("coding_dictionary.csv", export_dir, overwrite = TRUE))

cat("Exported columns per model:\n")
print(table(model_coefficients$model))
```

The scoring function is written to `model_export/predict_from_csv.R`. It
expects data in which the model variables are already coded as in this
analysis (coding dictionary; age in years; income-to-poverty ratio capped
at 11).

```{cat, engine.opts = list(file = "model_export/predict_from_csv.R", lang = "r")}
# Predicted probability of past-year telehealth use from the exported
# coefficient tables (HINF 5001, Team 1 prediction models).
#
# data:  one row per respondent. Every variable the model uses must already
#        be coded as in the analysis (see coding_dictionary.csv): age in
#        years; pov_ratio capped at 11; categorical variables as character
#        or factor using the labels in factor_levels.csv.
# model: a model name in model_coefficients.csv, for example
#        "Stepwise BIC logistic".
predict_from_csv <- function(data, model, export_dir = "model_export") {
  read <- function(f) read.csv(file.path(export_dir, f), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  coefs <- read("model_coefficients.csv")
  coefs <- coefs[coefs$model == model, ]
  if (nrow(coefs) == 0) stop("Unknown model: ", model)
  factor_levels <- read("factor_levels.csv")
  factor_levels <- factor_levels[order(factor_levels$variable,
                                       factor_levels$level_order), ]
  knots <- read("spline_knots.csv")

  columns <- list()
  for (term in setdiff(unique(coefs$term), "(Intercept)")) {
    if (startsWith(term, "ns(")) {
      v <- sub("^ns\\(([^,]+),.*$", "\\1", term)
      k <- knots[knots$variable == v, ]
      basis <- splines::ns(data[[v]],
                           knots = k$value[k$type == "interior"],
                           Boundary.knots = k$value[k$type == "boundary"])
      for (j in seq_len(ncol(basis))) columns[[paste0(term, j)]] <- basis[, j]
    } else if (term %in% factor_levels$variable) {
      lev <- factor_levels$level[factor_levels$variable == term]
      x <- as.character(data[[term]])
      unknown <- setdiff(unique(x[!is.na(x)]), lev)
      if (length(unknown)) {
        stop("Unknown level(s) of ", term, ": ", paste(unknown, collapse = ", "))
      }
      for (l in lev[-1]) columns[[paste0(term, l)]] <- as.numeric(x == l)
    } else {
      columns[[term]] <- as.numeric(data[[term]])
    }
  }
  x <- do.call(cbind, columns)

  beta <- setNames(coefs$estimate, coefs$column)
  slope <- beta[names(beta) != "(Intercept)"]
  absent <- setdiff(names(slope), colnames(x))
  if (length(absent)) stop("Columns not built: ", paste(absent, collapse = ", "))
  eta <- beta[["(Intercept)"]] + drop(x[, names(slope), drop = FALSE] %*% slope)
  plogis(eta)
}
```

A short README is written alongside the files.

```{cat, engine.opts = list(file = "model_export/README.md", lang = "markdown")}
# Exported prediction models: past-year telehealth use (NHIS)

Models developed on the NHIS 2024 adult file (80% training split, seed 2026)
and temporally validated on the NHIS 2025 adult file. Generated by
`nhis_telehealth_prediction_final.Rmd`; see that document for methods.

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `model_coefficients.csv` | Intercept and coefficients (log-odds scale) of the theory-based, theory-based BIC and primary (stepwise BIC) logistic models, with standard errors; nonzero penalized coefficients of the two group lasso models (no standard errors) |
| `spline_knots.csv` | Interior and boundary knots of the natural splines `ns(age, df = 3)` and `ns(pov_ratio, df = 3)` (2024 training data) |
| `factor_levels.csv` | Levels of each categorical variable; the first level is the reference |
| `coding_dictionary.csv` | Rules that turn raw NHIS codes into the model variables, including nonresponse and skip handling |
| `predict_from_csv.R` | `predict_from_csv(data, model)`: predicted probabilities from the files above |
| `xgb_full_pool.json`, `xgb_features.csv`, `xgb_settings.csv` | XGBoost model (xgboost JSON format), its input columns (R `model.matrix` dummy coding) and tuning settings |

Input data must be coded as in the analysis: age in years, income-to-poverty
ratio capped at 11, categorical variables labelled as in `factor_levels.csv`.
Models were fit without survey weights. Predictions describe the NHIS adult
population of 2024–2025 and have not been validated outside this survey.
Raw NHIS files are not included; they are available from the National
Center for Health Statistics.
```

```{r model-export-check}
# Reproduce the 2025 predictions from the exported files alone.
scorer <- new.env()
sys.source(file.path(export_dir, "predict_from_csv.R"), envir = scorer)
export_check <- data.frame(model = unique(model_coefficients$model))
export_check$max_abs_difference <- vapply(export_check$model, function(m) {
  max(abs(scorer$predict_from_csv(validation_2025, m, export_dir) - prob_2025[[m]]))
}, numeric(1))

xgb_reloaded <- xgb.load(file.path(export_dir, "xgb_full_pool.json"))
export_check <- rbind(export_check, data.frame(
  model = "Full pool XGBoost",
  max_abs_difference = max(abs(
    predict(xgb_reloaded, xgb.DMatrix(xgb_matrix(validation_2025, pool_vars))) -
      prob_2025[["Full pool XGBoost"]]))
))
print(export_check, row.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(export_check$max_abs_difference < 1e-6)
list.files(export_dir)
```

# Limitations

* **Prior viewing of evaluation data.** In the current pipeline,
  development uses only 2024 training data and the list of 2025 variable
  names. Earlier iterations of this project, however, examined results in
  both the 2024 test set and the 2025 file (including before the decision
  to expand the predictor set), and the coding dictionary was drafted
  while viewing predictor distributions in the full 2024 file. Neither
  evaluation set should therefore be described as untouched or fully
  independent; the 2025 analysis is a temporal validation by the
  development team.
* **Scope of the validation.** The 2025 file tests transportability to the
  next year of the same survey and questionnaire, not to other
  populations or data sources.
* **What nested CV covers.** Nested CV repeats variable selection and model
  fitting inside folds, but not screening, coding or the outcome-proxy
  diagnostic (which uses training outcomes), and the inner CV of group
  lasso shares the spline basis of the outer training part. XGBoost tuning
  was not nested; its tuning scores are reported separately. Interaction
  and borderline-item analyses select on the full training set and report
  apparent CV values.
* **Uncertainty intervals.** Bootstrap intervals resample PSUs within
  strata for unweighted metrics of fixed models; they exclude uncertainty
  from training and selection and are not design-based intervals for
  weighted metrics.
* **Weights and missing data.** Models are fit unweighted; weighted metrics
  and a weighted refit are reported. Weighted results represent the
  complete-case population; the original weights do not correct for
  exclusion of respondents with missing predictors.
* **Coding and item classification.** The coding dictionary was checked
  against the 2024 and 2025 codebooks; the check should still be
  spot-checked by the team. Nonresponse is assigned to the most common
  category for items with little nonresponse, which can misclassify a small
  number of respondents. Excluding items whose answer a telehealth visit
  can produce is a judgment about question content; the outcome-proxy
  diagnostic can flag suspicious items but cannot prove that an unflagged
  item is free of leakage. Care-use and access items that passed the
  diagnostic are examined only in a sensitivity analysis.
* **Theory-based specification.** The 22 theory-based items are one
  operationalization of Andersen's model, not a standard variable set, and
  cover individual predisposing, enabling and need factors plus
  urban-rural classification, but not other contextual factors or health
  behaviors. Urban-rural classification was added after earlier analyses
  had shown it to be a strong predictor, so the theory-based set is not
  fully specified independently of the data.
* **Income and year-specific coding.** The income-to-poverty ratio is based
  on the first of 10 income imputations and is top-coded at 11 in 2024 and
  12 in 2025; it is capped at 11 for both years.
* **Selection stability.** Some selected items are not reselected in every
  fold or half-sample (see the stability tables); the primary model should
  be read as one good parsimonious model, not the unique correct one.
* **Post-selection inference.** Odds ratios and their intervals are
  conditional on the selected model, ignore the survey design, and
  describe associations, not causal effects.
* **Software environment.** Package versions are printed but not locked;
  other versions (notably of xgboost) may give slightly different results.

# Summary

* Item pool: `r nrow(screening)` items in the 2024 file, `r sum(screening$fielded_2025)` of them also fielded in 2025;
  `r length(pool_terms)` candidate terms after screening (including the 22
  theory-based terms); excluded by the outcome-proxy diagnostic:
  `r if (length(flagged_items)) paste(flagged_items, collapse = ", ") else "none"`.
* Primary model (stepwise BIC from the intercept-only model):
  `r length(bic_terms)` terms. Stepwise BIC within the theory-based items
  kept `r length(bic_theory_terms)` of `r length(andersen_terms)` terms.
* CV log loss (nested for selection procedures; XGBoost tuning score not
  ranked): theory-based all items `r sprintf("%.4f", cv_table$cv_logloss[1])`,
  theory-based BIC `r sprintf("%.4f", cv_table$cv_logloss[2])`, primary
  `r sprintf("%.4f", cv_table$cv_logloss[4])`, group lasso
  `r sprintf("%.4f", cv_table$cv_logloss[5])`.
* AUROC, 2024 test: theory-based `r sprintf("%.3f", test_results["Theory-based logistic", "AUROC"])`,
  theory-based BIC `r sprintf("%.3f", test_results["Theory-based BIC logistic", "AUROC"])`,
  primary `r sprintf("%.3f", test_results[primary_model, "AUROC"])`.
* AUROC, 2025: theory-based `r sprintf("%.3f", results_2025["Theory-based logistic", "AUROC"])`,
  theory-based BIC `r sprintf("%.3f", results_2025["Theory-based BIC logistic", "AUROC"])`,
  primary `r sprintf("%.3f", results_2025[primary_model, "AUROC"])`.
* 2025 survey-weighted calibration gap (observed − predicted) for the
  primary model: `r sprintf("%.2f", gap_table[primary_model, "gap_pp"])`
  percentage points (95% CI `r sprintf("%.2f", gap_table[primary_model, "lower_95"])`
  to `r sprintf("%.2f", gap_table[primary_model, "upper_95"])`).
* Exploratory interactions entering the primary model by forward BIC:
  `r paste(interactions[["Stepwise BIC"]]$added, collapse = ", ")`;
  2025 AUROC `r sprintf("%.4f", interaction_results$AUROC_2025[1])` without vs
  `r sprintf("%.4f", interaction_results$AUROC_2025[2])` with interactions.
